info.title: Model
info.description: The models trained every night, and how each one scores: every nightly attempt to better it, and every day it predicted. Read by /model and /model/<name>. Scores alone: an options model's nightly picks are served to signed-in readers, on /v1/private/model, as the Model API page says. Nothing here says how a model is built.

get.summary: The models, or one model's summary, history or track record
get.description: Four calls on one path. With no parameters, the listing, as JSON. With a Model from the listing and a Report, one of that model's reports: summary, its summary, as JSON; or history, one row per nightly attempt, or track-record, one row per day it predicted, each as a CSV string with a header row. Model and Report go together: either alone is a 400. Report=picks is a 403 here: an options model's picks are for signed-in readers, on /v1/private/model.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: A model's name, from the listing. Asked with Report.

parameters.name: Report
parameters.description: Which of the model's reports: summary, its summary, as JSON; history, one row per nightly attempt; or track-record, one row per day it predicted. Asked with Model.

200.description:
With no parameters, the listing. With Model and Report=summary, the model's summary, as an object. With Model and Report=history or track-record, a CSV string with a header row, oldest row first. Each score column is a number, or empty where a day has no such score.

history, one row per nightly attempt: day, the night it was trained; kind, nightly for a nightly update or weekly for a weekly retrain; went_live, true when it replaced the live version; held_out_days, the days it was tested on, the newest whose results were known, which it never trained on, each YYYY-MM-DD with a space between them; training_days, how many earlier days it trained on or used to decide when to stop, as one count; from format 6, trained_again, true when the attempt beat the baseline and then trained again with its held-out days before it went live, false when it was kept back or went live as it was tested, and empty for attempts made before format 6; from format 6 too, trained_again_seconds, how long a second run trained, to one decimal, the training alone, set even where it failed its check or was stopped by the night's deadline and the version as tested went live, and empty where none trained: an attempt kept back, a night with no time left to start one, and every attempt before format 6; and stopping_tested_loss and stopping_again_loss, the first and the second run's loss on the days the first run stopped on, the check the listing's live.fine_tune reports, each empty where there was no second run; started, when the attempt began, in UTC with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-16T07:58:10+00:00; training_seconds, the time spent training, reading the days included, to one decimal; total_seconds, from started until the attempt's scores are known, so its training and then scoring the held-out days for the attempt and for the live version, to one decimal; and each score of the attempt, of the live version and of the know-nothing baseline, all on the same held-out days: attempt_<score>, live_<score> and baseline_<score>. started, training_seconds and total_seconds are empty for attempts made before 2026-10-15.

track-record, one row per day the model predicted, written once that day is scored: day, the day the prediction was made; each score, as <score>; and the baseline's, as baseline_<score>. A day the model was not running has no row. From format 2, down_days and down_in_a_row: the check that took the live version down, on the day whose score set it off, and empty on every other row. While a model is down it predicts nothing, so its track record has no rows until a new version goes live. From format 6, tested_<score> for each of the task's scores: where the live version trained again with its held-out days, the version as it was tested predicts each day too, and these are its scores on the day's 1-day hold, beside the live version's; empty where the live version is the one that was tested. From format 3, an options model's track record has a set of columns for each hold, each score again as <score>_1d, <score>_5d and <score>_20d, and the baseline's as baseline_<score>_1d and so on. Its plain columns repeat the 1-day hold's. Each hold's set has the two scores its loss adds up too, each lower-is-better: profit_log_loss_1d, the log loss of the chance each option makes money, and gain_pinball_1d, the pinball loss of its gain, and so on, with the baseline's as baseline_profit_log_loss_1d and so on. The plain columns have neither. A day's 5 and 20-day columns are empty until those holds' sell days are in, 6 and 21 trading days after the day. From format 5, a stock model's track record has a set of columns for each hold too. Every column it had stays, with the same values, the 1-day hold's: among them stocks, how many stocks the day scored, and all_gain, the average gain of every stock with one, what a random pick got. Then, for each hold, columns ending _1d, _5d and _20d: stocks, all_gain and each score, loss's three parts among them, with the baseline's scores as baseline_<score>_1d and so on. The _1d columns repeat the plain ones. A day's 5 and 20-day columns are empty until their results are in, 6 and 21 trading days after the day. Then Combined, in columns ending _combined: loss, up_log_loss, beats_log_loss, move_pinball, auc_up, auc_beats and acc_up, each the average of the day's 1, 5 and 20-day ones, beside the same average of the baseline's, as baseline_loss_combined and so on. They are filled in with the day's 20-day result, about a month after the day. The top 10 has no Combined: a 20-day gain and a 1-day gain aren't the same kind of number. And it has down_hold, as an options model's does: the hold, in trading days, of the check that took the live version down, beside down_days and down_in_a_row.

The scores are each task's: from format 3 the listing's tasks name them, and a task that names none has the four of the stock models, loss, auc_up, auc_beats and acc_up. Loss is lower-is-better, and an attempt goes live only when its loss is no higher than the live version's. From format 6, it goes live when its loss beats the baseline's, and a history's live_<score> columns are the live version's scores as it was tested, before it trained again, so none of the held-out days is one it learned. Loss is three scores added up for a stock model, each lower-is-better, which a history and a track record carry under every prefix they carry a score under: up_log_loss, the log loss of whether each stock went up; beats_log_loss, the log loss of whether it beat the average stock; and move_pinball, the pinball loss of the size of its move. A coin flip scores 0.693 on each of the first two. The listing carries only loss.

From format 3 a stock model also has top10_gain, the average gain of each night's top 10, the 10 stocks it is surest will go up, bought at the 9:40 AM ask and sold at the 3:40 PM bid the same day, as a share of what they cost; and top10_wins, how many of each night's top 10 made money, 0 to 10. An options model has loss, which adds up, for each hold that is on, the log loss of its chance and the pinball loss of its gain; profit_auc, how well its chance ranks the options that made money above the ones that didn't, where 0.5 is a coin flip; and top10_gain and top10_wins, of each hold's 10 best options, bought at the 9:40 AM ask and sold at the 3:40 PM bid on the sell day. The baseline's top10_gain and top10_wins are those of everything the model could have picked: what a random pick got.

From format 5 a stock model predicts three holds, each scored on its own, beside its own baseline: the 1-day hold, how each stock moves from 9:40 AM to 3:40 PM on the next trading day, as before; and the 5 and 20-day holds, from 9:40 AM on the next trading day to 3:40 PM 5 or 20 trading days later, the same days as an options model's holds. A hold's top10_gain and top10_wins are of its own top 10, bought at the 9:40 AM ask and sold at the 3:40 PM bid on the hold's last day. A stock model's 1-day result comes in the next trading day, its 5-day result 6 trading days after the prediction, and its 20-day result and Combined 21. An attempt is still judged on the 1-day hold alone, so a stock model's history is as it was.

anyOf.description: Asked with no parameters: every task, every model with its latest scores, from 2026-10-15 on, format_version, and from format 4, average_days.

format_version.description: The layout every model report follows; a listing without it is format 0. 0: the listing and the reports as first published. 1: a history's started, training_seconds and total_seconds. 2: a model's down and behind, and a track record's down_days and down_in_a_row. 3: a task's scores; the top 10's scores, profit_auc and an options model's track record's hold columns; the hold of down and of each check in behind; and the picks. 4: the listing's average_days; a down's reason, and its days and in_a_row null where no check did it; and a live version's days. 5: a stock model's track record's hold and Combined columns, and its down_hold; the hold of a stock model's down and of each check in its behind; and each model's holds. It goes up with any change to the reports' keys or columns, or to what a value means, added columns included. A listing is published after every model's reports, so its format_version holds for every report read after it.

average_days.description: From format 4: how many of a model's latest scored days its score and baseline average, and how many it needs before it is no longer New. A listing before format 4 has none, and both are 20.

tasks.description: What the models predict, in the order /model lists them.

id.description: What a model names its task by.

description.description: One line: what is predicted, and when it is scored.

scores.description: From format 3: the scores its models have, in the order /model offers them. A task without it has the four of the stock models.

name.description: The name Model takes, and the last part of the model's address on the site, /model/<name>.

task.description: The id of the task it predicts.

started.description: The first day it predicted, as YYYY-MM-DD.

retired.description: The day it stopped being trained, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it still is.

scored_days.description: The rows of its track record: the days it predicted that have been scored.

live.description: The version making its predictions, or the last one that did, for a retired model or one whose live version was taken down.

since.description: The night it went live, as YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: first, while the model's first version is still live; otherwise whether a nightly update or a weekly retrain made it.

fine_tune.description: From format 6, the trainer's check of the version's second run, which trained it again with its held-out days, on the 3 days its first run stopped on, which the second run never trained on. A second run that fails leaves the first run live. null where there was no check, as for a version from before format 6.

by.description: The first run's loss on those days less the second run's: above 0 where the second run did better, below 0 where it did worse.

slack.description: How much worse the second run may do and still pass.

days.description: From format 4: what the live version learned from, or null where the trainer has no record of it. An update learns from the newest day and older days drawn at random, so its days can be spread out between first and last.

training.description: How many days it trained on. From format 6, for a version that trained again with its held-out days, every one of them, held-out days included.

stopping.description: How many days decided when it stopped training. From format 6, 0 for a version that trained again with its held-out days.

first.description: The oldest of all those days, as YYYY-MM-DD.

last.description: The newest of all those days, as YYYY-MM-DD.

held_out.description: From format 10: how the version did on the held-out days its go-live was decided on, which it never trained on, beside the version it replaced and the know-nothing baseline, all three scored on those days. null for a version with no row in its history.

days.description: The held-out days, oldest first, each YYYY-MM-DD.

loss.description: The version's loss on those days, as it was tested, before any second run.

replaced_loss.description: The loss of the version it replaced, on the same days; null for a first version, which replaced none.

baseline_loss.description: The know-nothing baseline's loss on those days.

went_live.description: The attempts that replaced the live version.

score.description: Each score averaged over the last average_days rows of its track record, or all of them while it has fewer. Null while it has none. The four stock scores are always there, null where the task does not have them, and the rest where it does. An options model's are its 1-day hold's, and from format 5 a stock model's are too: holds has each hold's.

loss.description: Lower is better. Three scores added up: a history and a track record carry each one, as up_log_loss, beats_log_loss and move_pinball, and the listing does not.

profit_auc.description: From format 3, for an options model: how well its chance ranks the options that made money above the ones that didn't.

top10_gain.description: From format 3: the average gain of each night's top 10, as a share of what they cost.

top10_wins.description: From format 3: how many of each night's top 10 made money, 0 to 10.

baseline.description: The know-nothing baseline's scores, averaged over the same days. Null while it has none. Its top10_gain and top10_wins are those of everything the model could have picked: what a random pick got.

loss.description: Lower is better. Three scores added up: a history and a track record carry each one, as up_log_loss, beats_log_loss and move_pinball, and the listing does not.

profit_auc.description: From format 3, for an options model: how well its chance ranks the options that made money above the ones that didn't.

top10_gain.description: From format 3: the average gain of each night's top 10, as a share of what they cost.

top10_wins.description: From format 3: how many of each night's top 10 made money, 0 to 10.

holds.description: From format 5: the model's scores on each of its holds, by how long each is held: 1d, 5d and 20d, and for a stock model combined, its three holds averaged. The model's own score and baseline are its 1d's. Left out before format 5.

1d.description: The 1-day hold, whose scores are the model's own score and baseline.

days.description: How many scored days it has: the days whose result for it is in.

score.description: Each of the task's scores, averaged over its own latest average_days scored days, or all of them while it has fewer. Null before its first.

baseline.description: The baseline's scores, averaged over the same days. Null before its first.

days.description: How many scored days it has: the days whose result for it is in.

score.description: Each of the task's scores, averaged over its own latest average_days scored days, or all of them while it has fewer. Null before its first.

baseline.description: The baseline's scores, averaged over the same days. Null before its first.

days.description: How many scored days it has: the days whose result for it is in.

score.description: Each of the task's scores, averaged over its own latest average_days scored days, or all of them while it has fewer. Null before its first.

baseline.description: The baseline's scores, averaged over the same days. Null before its first.

combined.description: A stock model's: each day's 1, 5 and 20-day scores averaged, filled in with the day's 20-day result, about a month after the day. It has no top10_gain or top10_wins: a 20-day gain and a 1-day gain aren't the same kind of number. An options model has none.

days.description: How many scored days it has: the days whose result for it is in.

score.description: Each of the task's scores, averaged over its own latest average_days scored days, or all of them while it has fewer. Null before its first.

baseline.description: The baseline's scores, averaged over the same days. Null before its first.

down.description: From format 2: null while its live version is live. Otherwise the trainer took the live version down, and the model predicts nothing until a new version beats the baseline on the days it was tested on. From format 4, reason says why.

since.description: The night it was taken down, as YYYY-MM-DD.

reason.description: From format 4: why it was taken down. worse: it kept doing worse than the baseline, and days and in_a_row name the check. not_ahead: its live version went live without beating the baseline. track_record: its track record showed nothing better than the baseline, even on the days the live version predicted itself. Left out before format 4, where every take-down is worse.

days.description: The check that took it down: 1 for each scored day on its own, or 5 or 20 for an average over its latest scored days. From format 4, null for a reason other than worse.

in_a_row.description: How many scored days in a row it was worse. From format 4, null for a reason other than worse.

hold.description: From format 3: the hold the check ran on, in trading days, for an options model, whose checks run on each hold, and from format 5 for a stock model too. From format 5, a take-down for worse or track_record names the hold it was on, and one for not_ahead names none, since an attempt is judged on the 1-day hold. Null, or left out, for a model with no holds.

behind.description: From format 2: one entry per check, as of the newest scored day. The checks today: each day 5 days in a row, the 5-day average 10 days in a row, and the 20-day average 5 days in a row. An options model has each of them for each hold, from format 3, and a stock model from format 5.

days.description: 1 for each scored day on its own, or 5 or 20 for an average over its latest scored days.

in_a_row.description: How many scored days in a row it has been worse than the baseline, or null until it has enough days.

limit.description: The count that takes the live version down.

hold.description: From format 3: the hold the check ran on, in trading days, for an options model, whose checks run on each hold, and from format 5 for a stock model too. Null, or left out, for a model with no holds.

anyOf.description: Asked with Model and Report=summary: one model's summary. No page reads it yet, so its fields are not listed here.
Asked with Model and Report=history or track-record: the report, as a CSV string with a header row.

list.summary: The listing, asked with no parameters

tasks.name: Next-day move
tasks.description: Whether each S&P 500 stock closes higher the next trading day, scored once that day's prices are in.

tasks.name: Next-week move
tasks.description: Whether each S&P 500 stock closes higher five trading days on, scored once those prices are in.

tasks.name: Option picks
tasks.description: For every S&P 500 option, the chance it makes money if bought at 9:40 AM the next trading day and sold at 3:40 PM 1, 5 or 20 trading days later, after the gap between the buy and sell prices, scored once each hold's sell day is in.

models.name: pt-gnn
models.description: Reads the day's Training Graph build.

models.name: pt-gnn-5day
models.description: Reads the last five days of Training Graph builds.

models.name: tables-gnn-5day
models.description: Reads the last five days of query tables.

models.name: weekly-gnn
models.description: Reads the day's query tables, a week ahead.

models.name: pt-options
models.description: Reads the day's Training Graph build.

list-holds.summary: The listing from format 5: each model's scores on each hold, a stock model's with Combined, the 5-day hold's in for five days and the 20-day hold's and Combined for none yet

tasks.name: Stock moves
tasks.description: For each S&P 500 stock, the chance it goes up, the chance it beats the average stock, and how far it moves, from 9:40 AM the next trading day to 3:40 PM that day, or 5 or 20 trading days later, scored once each hold's last day is in.

tasks.name: Option picks
tasks.description: For every S&P 500 option, the chance it makes money if bought at 9:40 AM the next trading day and sold at 3:40 PM 1, 5 or 20 trading days later, after the gap between the buy and sell prices, scored once each hold's sell day is in.

models.name: tables-gnn-2
models.description: A second model of the day's query tables.

models.name: pt-options
models.description: Reads the day's Training Graph build.

list-held-out.summary: The listing from format 10: each live version's held_out, its loss on the days its go-live was decided on beside the version it replaced and the baseline's, pt-options' ahead of both and pt-gnn's of the baseline alone

tasks.name: Stock moves
tasks.description: Each S&P 500 stock's move from 9:40 AM on the next trading day to 3:40 PM that day, or 5 or 20 trading days later, scored once the last day's prices are in.

tasks.name: Option picks
tasks.description: Each S&P 500 option's chance of making money, bought at the 9:40 AM ask on the next trading day and sold at the 3:40 PM bid 1, 5 or 20 trading days later, scored once the sell day's prices are in.

models.name: pt-gnn
models.description: Graph neural network trained on each day's whole graph

models.name: pt-options
models.description: Graph neural network that scores every S&P 500 option on each day's whole graph

history.summary: Model=pt-gnn-5day&Report=history: its nine nightly attempts, the last two with times

track-record-holds.summary: Model=tables-gnn-2&Report=track-record: a stock model's ten scored days from format 5, each hold in its own columns and Combined in its own, the 5-day hold's in for five and the 20-day hold's and Combined for none yet

option-picks-track-record.summary: Model=pt-options&Report=track-record: an options model's nine scored days, each hold in its own columns, the 5-day hold's in for five and the 20-day hold's for none yet

400.description: Model without Report, or the other way round; a Report the API does not keep; any other parameter, even a lowercase model; or any of them given twice.

together.summary: Model without Report, or a Report the API does not keep

report.error: Model and Report go together, and Report is summary, history, track-record or picks.

other.summary: Any other parameter, even a lowercase model

report.error: Model, Report and Ticker are the only parameters.
Model, Report and Ticker may each be given once.

403.description: Report=picks: an options model's picks are for signed-in readers, on /v1/private/model, with the reader's ID token. See the Model API page.

picks.summary: Report=picks, which this path answers to no one

report.error: The picks are for signed-in readers, at /v1/private/model.

404.description: Model names no model in the listing.

report.error: There is no model named nope.

502.description: The listing or a report could not be read, or a summary, history or track record has not been published yet, even for a model the listing names.

report.summary: A report that could not be read

report.error: The track record of pt-gnn-5day could not be read.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this address in a few minutes: today 100 in 5 minutes, and an answer from the cache counts too. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then ask again. The report says the limit and the window in force, which can change: read them rather than assume today's.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again: the window the limit is counted over.

limit.description: How many requests one address may make in the window.

window_seconds.description: The window the requests are counted over, in seconds.

report.error: Too many requests from this address. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
